note: One entry per dispatch printed on the page, in page order: twelve cards (1-12) and twelve briefs (13-24). Every URL was opened during the build and carries a 24 November 2026 date stamp, quoted in date_on_page. The rule applied: a dispatch stands if the event happened on 24 November 2026 in some time zone. Six dispatches that were printed in an earlier draft are listed under held_back with their citations: the brief column was cut from eighteen to twelve so that every sentence could be set at 15 pixels in two columns, and an eighteen-item list at 11 pixels was unreadable on a thumbnail. The sheet therefore carries twenty-four dispatches, and the masthead, the map and this file all say twenty-four. Cards print a headline at 24 pixels in at most three lines; where a figure or an attribution would not fit, the card drops it and the attribution field below records the page's wording. Three dispatches from an early draft were dropped outright for want of a page dated 24 November (Paris, Jakarta, Kanton), and two were re-sourced when their pages failed a date check (London: The Standard's page is dated 25 November, now Anadolu; Suva: Post Courier returned HTTP 403). Taipei, Alamata, Moscow, Mexico City and the Canberra treaty slot were replaced earlier for the reasons recorded in the repository history; the Canberra slot now carries the Singapore-Australia leaders' meeting held there on 24 November.

stories.headline: Iran says mines hit three tankers
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The Guard navy said three tankers hit mines'. The mine strikes are the Revolutionary Guard navy's account, carried by Iranian state media. The card prints that account and its figure of three tankers at 24 pixels; it has no line left for the separate U.S. Treasury measure widening sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian firms, which is recorded here rather than asserted on the page.

stories.headline: Houthi strike hits Riyadh tower, Saudis say
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Yemen's Houthi fighters struck the tallest tower in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, on Tuesday for the second time in less than a week, wounding at least 11 people.' Quote: 'The Saudi-led coalition ... said later on Tuesday that the attack was carried out with a drone.' The card's word 'drone' is the coalition's account, not the page's assertion, and the toll of at least 11 is Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense figure; neither attribution fits the card at 24 pixels, so both are here.

stories.headline: 23 injured after car bomb explodes outside government offices in Colombia
stories.attribution: The toll is attributed to 'authorities' on the page, which names no claim of responsibility. The card prints 'at regional offices'; the page says the bomb exploded 'outside regional government offices', and the deck shortens that to fit one line at 13.5 pixels.

stories.headline: How major US stock indexes fared Tuesday 11/24/2026
stories.publisher: The Globe and Mail, carrying The Associated Press markets table
stories.attribution: Index levels and percentage moves are the Associated Press table's closing figures, carried by The Globe and Mail. The card prints the three moves and drops the Dow's closing level of 50,018.70, which the table gives.

stories.headline: Democrat Victoria Broderick unseats eight-term Republican incumbent in Tennessee
stories.attribution: The report gives 259 House seats, resting on the Associated Press race call it cites. The card prints that figure as the fact; Victoria Broderick's win in the 4th district, which the page leads on, does not fit a three-line headline at 24 pixels and is recorded here.

stories.headline: Lower House passes fiscal bill in decisive vote
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Brazil's Lower House approved the government's fiscal adjustment bill on Monday (Nov. 23) by a decisive 353-128 vote'. The ballot was cast on 23 November; this report of it is dated 24 November. The card prints the vote and drops the page's line that the real weakened to around R$6 per dollar.

stories.headline: Volkswagen labor talks end without deal as union warns of January strikes
stories.attribution: The strike warning is IG Metall's; the no-deal account is the union's and the company's. The card's sub-line says strikes could begin on 1 January, which is the union's warning, not a decision.

stories.headline: DR Congo: Concern for trapped Ebola workers as violence against women and girls deepens
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Staff from the World Health Organization (WHO) and Ebola responders remain trapped in a hospital in Ituri province ... the UN agency said'. Quote: 'The health workers have been sheltering in a maternity ward since fighting began on Saturday'. The card prints who is trapped; the maternity ward and the day the fighting began are here, not on the page.

stories.headline: Three Palestinians Martyred, Five Injured in Khan Younis Strike
stories.attribution: The toll is the one Jordan News reported, and the card credits that paper in its headline because the page does not attribute the figure to a monitor. Five wounded and the site, al-Mawasi, are on the page and do not fit a three-line headline; they are recorded here.

stories.printed_headline: IRAQ PM MOVES ON KURDISH OIL
stories.headline: Iraq Moves To Take Control Of Oilfields, Border Crossings In Kurdish Region
stories.attribution: The order is the prime minister's, as reported: the Oil Ministry to take over oilfields and border forces to shut unofficial crossings. The page describes an instruction, not a completed takeover, and carries no Kurdish reaction. The card prints the oilfields; the crossings are recorded here.

stories.headline: China's Shenzhou-24 mission launches 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The Shenzhou-24 mission lifted off today (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. ET.' Quote: 'That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit.' The card prints China, the nationality and the orbit. The mission name is not on the card: 'SHENZHOU-24' is a single word 242 pixels wide, wider than a card's 227, so it cannot be set at 24 pixels; Tiangong, and the fact that Ali is the first person from Pakistan in orbit, are recorded here.

stories.headline: 11th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting, 24 November 2026
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Prime Minister and Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese held the 11th Singapore-Australia Annual Leaders' Meeting (ALM) in Canberra today.' Quote: 'Key outcomes of the ALM included the signing of the landmark Agreement on Transboundary Movement of Carbon Dioxide Streams for the Purposes of Offshore Geological Sequestration; the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on Essential Supplies'. The card prints the CO2 pact in two names and drops the supplies memorandum; 'landmark' and 'first-of-its-kind' are the statement's own words and are not printed.

stories.headline: EU imposes hard import quotas on Chinese hybrid cars, sweeping in UK and Japan
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Announced by the European Commission, the 200-day provisional safeguard is designed to shield European automakers from a 49% surge in hybrid imports'. Quote: 'capping shipments from China while sweeping in major auto exporters including the United Kingdom, Japan, Turkey, and South Korea.' The brief prints the measure and China, its main target; the sweep-in of the UK, Japan, Turkey and South Korea, and the 49% surge, are here.
stories.printed_brief: EU sets 200-day quotas on hybrid cars from China.

stories.headline: Putin says Russia's response to Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries inevitable
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Russian President Vladimir Putin said Tuesday that Moscow's response to Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries was inevitable.' Quote: 'retaliatory actions on our part are inevitable.' The brief keeps the word 'inevitable' as the page prints it, in quotation marks' stead by attribution to Putin. This page replaces a TRT World article that displayed no date; the words are the same report.
stories.printed_brief: Putin: retaliation for refinery strikes is inevitable.

stories.headline: Russian overnight attack injures 22 in Zaporizhzhia
stories.attribution: The two dead and 22 wounded are a regional defence official's figures, as reported. The brief calls that official a Ukraine official, which is what the page describes.
stories.printed_brief: Strike kills two and wounds 22, Ukraine official says.

stories.headline: London Tube drivers to go on strike as talks over working conditions fail
stories.attribution: Quote: 'the union will launch a series of rolling 24-hour strikes beginning on Thursday'. The brief's 'Tube drivers' and 'Thursday' are the page's; the union is the RMT, which the brief does not name. This page replaces a Standard article that turned out to be dated 25 November.
stories.printed_brief: Tube drivers to start 24-hour strikes on Thursday.

stories.headline: Nigerian state imposes curfew after four killed at political rally
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Authorities have imposed a curfew in Nigeria's southern Delta state after four opposition supporters were killed at a political rally on Monday.' The brief says 'four die at rally', the page's own label for the event; the page calls the dead 'opposition supporters' and places the rally and the curfew in Delta state, so the pin sits there rather than at the AFP dateline, Lagos. The curfew is the state government's, announced by its secretary; the four deaths were confirmed by aviation minister Festus Keyamo. This replaces an Alamata dispatch: the page there said Amnesty's findings were 'published late on Monday', i.e. 23 November.
stories.printed_brief: Delta state declares curfew after four die at rally.

stories.headline: Outrage as 28 women, girls abducted, 15 cases of sexual violence against minors reported in Sudan's Blue Nile state
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The Strategic Initiative for Women in the Horn of Africa (SIHA Network) has reported the abduction of 28 women and girls fleeing fighting in Damazin'. Quote: 'fighters from the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied militias had abducted the women and girls'. The brief says 'a group says', which is the SIHA Network; the state is the Blue Nile, as the page has it. No monitor's tally is cited.
stories.printed_brief: Group says 28 women and girls abducted in Blue Nile.

stories.headline: Singapore upgrades GDP forecast to around 6% for 2026, expects growth to moderate in 2027
stories.attribution: Quote: "Singapore's economy grew 6.1 per cent year-on-year in the third quarter, beating its advance estimate of 5.4 per cent". The brief calls the body 'Singapore' and prints the two figures; the page names the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), as does its release at meti.gov.sg dated 24 November 2026.
stories.printed_brief: Singapore Q3 growth 6.1%, ahead of 5.4% estimate.

stories.headline: Japan boosts ICC funding amid US sanctions threat
stories.attribution: Payment of Japan's 2027 dues by year-end is Japan's pledge; the April sanctions deadline is the U.S. measure's, as reported. The brief says 'before US sanctions', which is the page's sequence; it drops the year-end deadline for the payment.
stories.printed_brief: Japan to pay 2027 ICC dues before US sanctions.

stories.headline: Philippine Forces Train to Secure Luzon Strait with Warships, BrahMos Missiles
stories.attribution: Quote: 'Philippine forces are practicing how to secure the Luzon Strait through the deployment of warships and a BrahMos missile battery for maritime strike operations this month.' The brief says 'drills', the page's 'practicing'. This replaces a Taipei market report from an auto-generated site.
stories.printed_brief: Philippines drills to hold Luzon Strait with BrahMos.

stories.headline: Gas explosion in Hanoi kills six, injures 10
stories.attribution: The toll and the description of a suspected gas explosion at an eatery are officials' account as reported; the gas leak is the likely cause, not a finding. The brief keeps 'suspected' out of its line for want of room and says 'gas blast'.
stories.printed_brief: Gas blast at Hanoi eatery kills six, injures 10.

stories.headline: Xiamen Airlines signs deal for 50 Boeing 737-8s
stories.attribution: The $7.4bn is the list price of the order, not a disclosed payment, and the page reports the order as pending approval. The brief prints the list price and drops the pending approval.

stories.headline: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
stories.attribution: Quote: 'The International Court of Justice ... last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority'. The 6,803 figure is in the page's headline. A final ruling, not a pending case. The brief drops the ICJ ruling for want of a line.
stories.printed_brief: Malaysia to send 6,803 more Myanmar nationals home.

held_back.headline: Ontario Announces Bold Plan to Build Mines Faster
held_back.publisher: Government of Ontario newsroom (Ministry of Energy and Mines)
held_back.why_held_back: The page's wording is 'intends to introduce ... that, if passed, would fast-track'; nothing is law. Held back when the brief column was cut from eighteen to twelve, because a bill that is only an intention is the least of the day's news.

held_back.headline: Latvian President sees potential turning point in Ukraine war next year
held_back.why_held_back: The forecast is President Edgars Rinkevics's: a tipping point that could come in spring or summer. Held back with the brief column's cut to twelve.

held_back.headline: West Africa: Gold Refining Projects Already Exceed Mining Production
held_back.why_held_back: Quote: 'According to a Reuters survey published on Tuesday, November 24, the capacities of projects launched or announced since 2024 exceed 1,000 tons per year, while regional production is estimated at 585 tons.' The page names no city. Held back with the brief column's cut to twelve.

held_back.headline: South Korea scrambles jets as Russian warplanes enter air defense zone
held_back.why_held_back: The scramble and the incursion are South Korea's account, as reported; no airspace violation was reported. Held back because the Manila drill covers the same beat.

held_back.headline: Hasina's December 16 homecoming plan: Bangladesh says ex-PM can be brought back only through extradition
held_back.why_held_back: The 16 December plan is Sheikh Hasina's announcement; the position that she can only be brought back by extradition is a state minister's. Held back with the brief column's cut to twelve.

held_back.headline: 'When it mattered' Australia failed Pacific at COP31, elders say
held_back.why_held_back: Quote: '"When it mattered, Australia has sided with the fossil fuel producers and lobbyists," the group said in a statement.' The statement is the Pacific Elders' Voice's. Held back with the brief column's cut to twelve.
